calls.title: Skyscanner + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The team discussed critical pricing details, including a negotiated annual platform fee of $100,000 and user pricing set at $1,250, with volume discounts starting at 50 users. Gaps in discounts between 200 and 400 users were identified for review. Skyscanner aims to increase annual experiments from 1,200 to 2,000, emphasizing speed and quality while reducing maintenance efforts. The analysis phase of experiments currently takes an average of 27 days, signaling a bottleneck that needs addressing—Christian highlighted Growth Book's templates as a potential solution. The trial account expires in 17 days, with a proof of concept due by the end of Q3, and onboarding of 50 users targeted for Q4. Ongoing collaboration and clear communication are essential for the partnership's progression.
calls.keywords: experimentation, pricing, business case, discounting, evaluation timeline, licensing

calls.title: Skyscanner + GrowthBook
calls.summary: The discussion centered on establishing a flexible, scalable pricing model for Skyscanner, particularly focusing on a 12-month contract with an initial activation of 50 licenses in Q4, aiming for a total of 300-400 users by July. The team emphasized the need for a pricing structure that balances flexibility with accountability, favoring a flat fee model over tiered pricing. The platform fee was confirmed at $100,000, significantly lower than fees for other enterprises, covering vital support and research services. Participants stressed the importance of clear documentation on services, including SLAs, technical support, and customer success resources. Lastly, a follow-up meeting was scheduled to refine proposals and ensure Skyscanner's internal users' commitments align with their needs.
calls.keywords: experimentation scaling, pricing model, platform fee, license ramp-up, POC, customer support SLAs
